raw_response:
My land is 7.5 mu. Most of it I put to cotton like always — that is my cash. A small piece, about two and a half mu, I keep for wheat and maize so we have flour and grain at home. My old woman and I only need so much. I have been doing it this way for many years, same as my father.

For cotton, I follow what I did last year. Before planting in April, I plough the field deep — cotton roots go down far, so I do not use the rotary alone. I spread two bags of diammonium before I sow — about one bag for every two and a half mu. Then when the plants come up waist-high, I put one bag of urea between every two mu. My neighbor Old Wang puts a little more urea, but urea is expensive this year, I keep it like before. I buy the Bt cotton seed from the dealer in town. Everyone around here uses Bt now, the bollworm used to eat us alive before.

I water from the well four times for cotton — once before planting if dry, then at budding, flowering, and boll-filling. Cotton brings many pests, I spray six, seven times — aphid, mite, whitefly, bollworm still comes sometimes. Last year I got about 250 jin... no, about 250 kilos of seed cotton per mu. Not bad.

Wheat I planted already last October. In spring when it greens up I spread one bag of urea across the small plot. I water twice — once after green-up, once when the head comes out. Wheat here does not have many bugs, one spray is enough. I get maybe 400 kilos per mu, enough flour for us and some to sell.

After wheat I plant maize in June, right into the stubble, no tilling — saves time and diesel. Hybrid seed from the dealer. One bag of compound at planting, then urea when it reaches my knee. Two waterings, spray once for borer. Maybe 450 kilos per mu.
